Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Parity Shift: Political Action
Select a Methuselah who has more pool than you.
Divide up to X of *that* pool among all of the
Methuselahs as you see fit, where X is the
number of Methuselahs in the game.

Is that : divide up to X of the difference
or : divide up to X of the whole pool

e.g.: I have 3 pool, my prey has 6, and there are
five Methuselahs in the game. Can I divide up
five of my prey's pool, or only three?

L. Scott Johnson

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
dhu...@ic1d.harris.com (Dale Hurtt) writes:

>In article <3eean7$k...@redwood.cs.scarolina.edu>,




>X is the number of Methuselahs in the game therefore, divide up 5 pool.

>"That pool" refers to the pool of the Methuselah you have selected, not
>your pool.

The "That Pool" can also be correctly interpretted (as far as grammar is
involved) to refer to the "more pool" - i.e. the excess itself.
My example was unfortunately ambiguous, try:

e.g.: I have 2 pool, my prey has 6, and there are

five Methuselahs in the game. Can I divide up

five of my prey's pool, or only four (six minus two)?

We currently play the way you suggest, I was just wondering what the
rulling was on the other interpretation.

L. Scott
